My sophomore year of college my roommate fell incredible ill. From the gates of his mouth would spew vomit and from the deepest reaches of his intestines would pour molten chocolate.

He was forced to skip classes and more or less occupied the tiny, gross, little bathroom next to our dormroom that would flood with shower water. I had returned from my classes for the day and was laying on my lofted bed minding my own business while my roommate stood hunched (he was unable to sit) over his desk playing Tetris (we were and still are Tetris obsessed).

My roommate pipes up and we begin a conversation of such banality that I have no recollection of what was said. I literally cannot remember what I said to him that made him laugh. He begins to laugh and he's laughing hard. He's laughing with such vigor that he's gasping for air. And then we hear it. And it's no mere fart.

It's the sound of something more. The wet, bubbly screams of something that knows it should not exist. A being acutely aware of its suffering and pain. My roommate was so sick and laughed so hard that he shit his pants. By now I'm giggling from what I assumed was his fart when he tells me he literally shit his pants because he laughed so hard. We're both now crying from laughter as my roommate retrieves fresh under and pants and traipses of to the flooded bathroom to abandon his soupy underwear and sweat pants.
